title: dispatchRoute
summary: Dispatch one server loader or action from a Request.

sections.title: Parameters
sections.body: request must contain the normalized application route URL, not the transport endpoint URL. Pass the server route table. document defaults to false: data responses use private, no-store and encode redirects for browser transport. document: true preserves document redirect/status behavior.

sections.title: Returns
sections.body: Returns a Promise<Response>; GET selects a loader and mutations select an action.

sections.title: Usage
sections.body: Dispatch one server loader or action from a Request.

sections.title: Behavior and limits
sections.body: Call only on the server. Route misses return 404 and missing handlers return 405. Server-only implementations must not enter browser bundles.

sections.title: Request security
sections.body: Since 0.5.2, mutations accept POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE only. Other unsafe methods return 405 before actions run. An Origin must exactly match the request URL origin; opaque or foreign origins and Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site return 403. Headerless server clients remain supported. Authentication, authorization and CSRF tokens remain application responsibilities. Behind a reverse proxy, construct the Request with the public URL or configure Express protocol/trust proxy for your trusted proxy only. Smolter does not trust forwarded headers automatically. Enforce body-size and request-time limits before handing the raw stream to Smolter; do not consume it with a body parser.

sections.title: Public error data
sections.body: Since 0.5.2, Smolter transfers only an error’s name/message and explicit HTTP status, statusText and data. Arbitrary Error metadata, request configurations, causes, stacks and custom toJSON hooks are not copied into route-data responses or hydration snapshots. Treat error messages, explicit Response bodies and route-error data as public. Keep credentials and internal diagnostics in server-side logs, and do not render them from a custom error boundary. If browser code relied on custom Error properties, move intentionally public fields into explicit route-error data or a Response payload.
